and asked from him assistance through prayer,
that God might restore to him the inheritance of his fathers.
And when he had prayed over him,
he gave him as a blessing the price of a horse.
And when he had acquired a mount,
twelve Armenian men attached themselves to him,
and they went first against the fortress called Amuda.
And when the men of the fortress saw the son of their lord,
they quickly surrendered the fortress to him,
and he entered and killed the Greeks who were in it.
And the dread of him fell upon the Greeks who were in the rest of the fortresses,
and rapidly he seized many places.
And Armenians and Franks united with him,
and he encountered the Turks,
and slaughtered about three thousand of them.
And he triumphed,
and made a name for himself.
And the Turks were wary of him,
and did not attack him at all.
Then he also ruled over cities,
Anazarba and the rest.
And in this year, Nur al-Din, son of Zengi, took Apamea and other fortresses from the Franks.
And the lord of Antioch set an ambush for him,
and killed many of his army.
And Nur al-Din himself, with a few men, escaped,
and they entered Aleppo.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and sixty,
1460 of the Greeks,
which is the year five hundred and forty-three,
543 of the Arabs,
Nur al-Din marched against Harem,
and took captive its district,
and destroyed the edifices that were outside its fortress.
And when the Prince, the lord of Antioch, went out to drive him away from Harem,
the Franks were defeated by the Turks,
and the Prince was killed,
he who was more feared by the Turks than all the Frankish kings.
And when dissension broke out among the people of Antioch,
many of them wished to surrender it to Nur al-Din.
Then other people hastily sent to the King of Jerusalem,
and he quickly arrived,
and encouraged the remnant of the knights who were left,
and appointed their Patriarch as administrator over them,
until Bohemond, the son of the Prince who had been killed, should grow up.
And the lord of Kesoun was also killed at this time,
and Joscelin became ruler over Kesoun and over the fortresses.
And in that year also, the son of Mas‘ud, the Sultan of Iconium,
whose name was Qilij Arslan,
encamped against Marash,
and took it from the Franks.
